title: Warm Chinese Egg Century Egg Congee
description: A floral and tender Chinese dish featuring thyme, perfect for a crowd, this Buddhist-temple-friendly congee is a delight to eat. It is made with century eggs and served on a wooden board.
instructions: Rinse the rice in a fine mesh sieve until the water runs clear.
In a large pot, combine the rice and water, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes, or until the rice has broken down and the mixture has a creamy consistency.
While the congee is cooking, heat the sesame oil in a small pan over medium heat.
Add the grated ginger and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Add the chopped scallions and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Stir the cooked ginger and scallion mixture into the congee.
Add the sliced century eggs, thyme, salt, and pepper to the congee, and stir to combine.
Push the congee to one side of the pot, and add a little water to the other side if necessary to create a well.
Pour the beaten eggs into the well, and scramble them until they are cooked through.
Mix the eggs into the congee, and serve hot on a wooden board.
